description: Work container vessels at the 3 T1 berths: crane work queues, container moves, lashing, tally and completion messages to carriers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A vessel call has a fixed berth window of about 18 to 36 hours; past one shift of manual working the carrier misses its window and the next port call. Container location and hazardous cargo stowage must be current to load safely. About $157,000 of T1 revenue a day comes from vessel handling
manual_workaround: Paper bay plans and load lists from the carrier; crane work queues run by radio from the shift superintendent; paper tally; reconcile in the TOS after recovery. Workable for about one shift at about 40% of normal crane productivity
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-03; SYS-05; SYS-07; SYS-08; SYS-10
dependent_third_parties: Ocean carriers; longshore hiring hall; T1 crane OEM
dependent_people_or_facilities: Vessel planners; shift superintendents; longshore labor; T1 berths
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,700 container moves a day with 2 vessels at berth on average; manual working cuts crane productivity by about 60%
quantified_regulatory_impact: Hazardous cargo stowage must follow the dangerous cargo manifest; a missed reportable cyber incident report under 33 CFR 6.16-1 would add a regulatory failure
safety_impact: Severe: unsafe crane motion or a heavy or hazardous container mis-stowed if TOS data is wrong
subpart_f_linkage: Critical IT (SYS-01) and critical OT (SYS-03) to be designated in the Cybersecurity Plan; backups of both required (101.650(g)(4))

description: In-gate and out-gate for about 3,000 truck transactions a day on 12 lanes: TWIC check, OCR of container, chassis and plate, appointment and customs hold check, interchange receipt
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Trucks queue onto port roads within about 90 minutes of a gate stop and the port authority can close the approach. Releasing a container on a customs hold is a regulatory failure, so the gate stops rather than guesses. Gate transactions must not be lost (RPO 1 h)
manual_workaround: Manual gate on 3 lanes with clerks keying container numbers against a printed release list; TWIC checked by security officers; paper interchange receipts; import deliveries limited to containers confirmed released. About 25% of normal throughput
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-04; SYS-05; SYS-07; SYS-08; SYS-14
dependent_third_parties: Trucking companies; customs data exchange service; OCR vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Gate and yard clerks; security officers; T1 gate complex
quantified_operational_impact: About 3,000 transactions a day (about 190 an hour at peak); manual gate handles about 50 an hour
quantified_regulatory_impact: Customs hold status must be honored at every release; TWIC access control at the gate is an FSP measure (33 CFR Part 105)
safety_impact: Moderate: truck queues on public roads create traffic safety hazards
subpart_f_linkage: Critical IT (SYS-02); TWIC readers support the FSP access control measures

business_process: Yard, equipment dispatch and reefer monitoring
description: Container inventory and location, RTG and yard tractor dispatch through VMTs, remote monitoring of 1,200 reefer plugs, and moves between berth, yard and gate
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without current locations containers are lost in the stacks and moves slow sharply. Reefers must be checked by hand every 4 hours when monitoring is down, which needs about 8 extra technicians per shift. Yard data can be rebuilt by a physical yard check, but that takes 2 shifts at T1
manual_workaround: Printed yard inventory from the last export; radio dispatch; manual reefer checks every 4 hours; physical yard check if data is lost
dependent_third_parties: T1 crane OEM; reefer monitoring vendor; SD-WAN provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Yard clerks; RTG and yard tractor operators; reefer technicians
quantified_operational_impact: About 34,000 containers in the yard on an average day, including up to 1,200 reefers; manual reefer checks need 8 extra technicians per shift
quantified_regulatory_impact: Cargo claims for reefer temperature loss are contractual, not regulatory
safety_impact: Moderate: unplanned equipment moves and manual dispatch raise collision risk in the stacks
subpart_f_linkage: Reefer monitoring gateways are OT to be inventoried and designated (101.650(b)(3))

business_process: Security, access control and hazardous cargo control
description: TWIC-based access to secure areas, CCTV and perimeter video analytics, security patrols, and the dangerous cargo location list used by the FSOs and emergency responders
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Emergency responders must be able to find hazardous cargo at any time, and FSP access control must continue at every MARSEC level (33 CFR Part 105). A failure could contribute to a transportation security incident
manual_workaround: Security officers check TWICs visually and log entries by hand; printed dangerous cargo location list at each shift change; CCTV recorders keep recording locally if the network is down; extra patrols
dependent_third_parties: Port authority police and fire; Captain of the Port for each terminal; CCTV integrator
dependent_people_or_facilities: Security officers; FSOs; gate complexes and yards
quantified_operational_impact: About 3,600 TWIC entries a day across both terminals; manual checks need 6 extra officers per shift
quantified_regulatory_impact: A failure of FSP access control is a breach of security reportable under 33 CFR 101.305(b); records of incidents and breaches must be kept (105.225(b)(3))
safety_impact: Severe: responders cannot locate hazardous cargo, or an unauthorized person enters a secure area
subpart_f_linkage: PACS, TWIC readers and CCTV support the FSPs; the CySO decides in the Plan whether they are critical IT

business_process: Crane and equipment maintenance and OT support
description: Maintain STS cranes, RTGs, mobile harbor cranes, reach stackers and yard tractors; manage PLC and HMI programs, the crane management system and vendor diagnostics
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cranes run on local controllers and can work without the TOS, but a crane with a corrupted PLC program cannot work at all. Each T1 STS crane carries about 14% of T1 crane capacity; each T2 mobile harbor crane about half of T2 capacity. PLC programs change rarely, so the RPO is the last approved program version
manual_workaround: Operate cranes in local mode with operators in the cab; isolate the crane network; reload controller programs from the offline copies (T1) or from the OEM (T2)
dependent_third_parties: T1 crane OEM; T2 mobile harbor crane OEM
dependent_people_or_facilities: Mechanics, crane electricians and controls technicians; crane electrical houses
quantified_operational_impact: 7 STS cranes, 24 RTGs and 2 mobile harbor cranes; one crane reload by the T2 OEM takes 1 to 3 days today
quantified_regulatory_impact: A cyber incident affecting crane controllers is reportable immediately under 33 CFR 6.16-1
safety_impact: Severe: unsafe crane or RTG motion if controller logic or safety limits are altered
subpart_f_linkage: Critical OT; PLC programs and HMI settings must be backed up and protected (101.650(g)(4)); remote access needs a documented justification (101.650(e)(3)(v))

business_process: Breakbulk, project cargo and vehicle vessel operations
description: Work breakbulk, project cargo and roll-on/roll-off vessels at the 2 T2 berths: stowage, mobile harbor crane lifts, vehicle discharge and tally
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Breakbulk and vehicle work can run on paper tallies for longer than container work, but heavy-lift plans need current cargo data and crane availability. About $38,000 of T2 revenue a day comes from vessel handling
manual_workaround: Paper tallies and cargo lists from the customer; vehicle discharge tallied by VIN on handheld scanners in offline mode; mobile harbor cranes in local mode
dependent_third_parties: Breakbulk and vehicle logistics customers; longshore hiring hall; T2 mobile harbor crane OEM
dependent_people_or_facilities: T2 planners and superintendents; longshore labor; T2 berths
quantified_operational_impact: About 6 vessel calls a week; a vehicle carrier discharges about 1,500 units a call
quantified_regulatory_impact: Project cargo lift plans are safety documents under the company operations manual
safety_impact: Severe: heavy-lift or vehicle-handling plans based on wrong data
subpart_f_linkage: Critical IT and OT at T2 must be in the inventory and the network map (101.650(b)(3)-(4))

description: In-gate and out-gate for about 600 truck transactions a day on 4 lanes, vehicle release and car carrier loading
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Lower volume than T1, so queues build more slowly. Releasing cargo on a customs hold is a regulatory failure
manual_workaround: Manual gate on 2 lanes with a printed release list; TWIC checked by security officers
dependent_third_parties: Trucking companies; customs data exchange service; OCR vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: T2 gate clerks; security officers; T2 gate complex
quantified_operational_impact: About 600 transactions a day; manual gate handles about 30 an hour
quantified_regulatory_impact: Customs hold status must be honored at every release
subpart_f_linkage: Critical IT (T2 gate servers run an unsupported operating system, gap 11)

description: Receive release and hold status from the customs data exchange; exchange bay plans, load and discharge lists and container status with 16 carrier services and customers; vessel schedules and gate status with the two port community systems
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Holds and releases change during the day and drive both gates. Partners can resend the last 24 hours of messages, so data loss is recoverable, but an unreliable hold status stops import deliveries
manual_workaround: Check hold status through the customs data exchange web portal; carriers email bay plans and lists; port community systems updated through their web screens
dependent_third_parties: Ocean carriers; customs data exchange service; two port community systems
quantified_operational_impact: About 45,000 EDI messages a day; manual hold checks take about 2 minutes per container
quantified_regulatory_impact: Releasing a container on a customs hold is a regulatory failure; EDI carries confidential bills of lading and customs data
subpart_f_linkage: Critical IT; encryption of EDI traffic required when technically feasible (101.650(c)(2))

description: Berth scheduling, stowage and crane split planning, yard allocation, and the scheduling optimization service (AI-001)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Plans are prepared 24 to 72 hours before a vessel arrives, so planning can pause for a day. Plans made by hand need a second planner check for heavy and hazardous cargo
manual_workaround: Plan on carrier bay plans and spreadsheets; berth schedule on the whiteboard, shared by email and phone; the optimization service is not needed for recovery
quantified_operational_impact: About 20 vessel plans a week across both terminals; manual planning takes about twice as long
quantified_regulatory_impact: Shipping Act: berth windows must not give undue or unreasonable preference (46 U.S.C. 41106; see P10)
safety_impact: Moderate: unsafe stowage or segregation if plans are not checked
subpart_f_linkage: SYS-12 designation decided in the Cybersecurity Plan (see P10)

description: Customer portal and truck appointment system (SYS-14): container availability, appointments for about 1,200 trucking companies, invoices and links to the hosted payment page
process_owner: Director of Commercial and Customer Service
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: T1 gate throughput depends on appointments; without them truck arrivals bunch and queues double. The carrier alliance expects the portal to be available as a service commitment (P09)
manual_workaround: Phone and email appointments recorded on a shared spreadsheet; availability list emailed to trucking companies every 2 hours
dependent_third_parties: Trucking companies; payment service provider; development contractor
quantified_operational_impact: About 2,800 appointments a day; manual booking needs 6 extra customer service staff
quantified_regulatory_impact: Contractual availability commitments to the carrier alliance (P09); no regulatory deadline

business_process: Empty container and chassis depot operations
description: Receive and release empty containers and chassis for carriers at the off-dock depot (about 400 truck transactions a day)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Empty returns can be diverted to the T1 gate for one day; carriers charge for missed empty repositioning
manual_workaround: Paper receipts; diversion of empty returns to T1; manual status messages to carriers
quantified_regulatory_impact: None beyond carrier contracts (the depot is not an MTSA facility)
subpart_f_linkage: Connected to the TOS; covered by the Plan as part of the network (101.650(b)(3))

description: Vessel and cargo handling invoices, storage and demurrage charges, collections
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Charges can be rebuilt from TOS move history, so billing can wait 72 hours. About $275,000 of invoicing is delayed for each day billing is down
manual_workaround: Queue invoices; rebuild charges from TOS move history; collect by check or through the payment service provider

description: Employee payroll, timekeeping, onboarding and termination
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; missing it has legal and retention impact. Longshore labor is paid through the hiring hall process, not company payroll
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider; paper timesheets
quantified_regulatory_impact: State and federal wage payment rules
subpart_f_linkage: Not critical IT; holds employee personal information (Fla. Stat. 501.171)

description: General ledger, procurement and vendor payments
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Vendor payments can wait a week; the business email compromise risk rises during any disruption
manual_workaround: Manual payment approvals with call-back verification

description: Customer service to carriers, trucking companies and cargo owners; vessel status notices; port authority liaison
process_owner: Director of Commercial and Customer Service
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Partners need status at least twice a day during any disruption; email may be unavailable in an incident
manual_workaround: Phone calls from the printed partner contact list; notices from a clean email account; portal banner
dependent_third_parties: Ocean carriers; port authorities; trucking companies
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,200 trucking companies and 16 carrier services and customers to update
quantified_regulatory_impact: Contract notice clauses in terminal services agreements
subpart_f_linkage: Communications with the COTP and port partners are part of the Plan (101.645(b))

description: Security monitoring (SIEM and OT monitoring), identity administration, backups, service desk
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Needed to detect attacks and to validate that restored systems are clean; the MSSP can operate from its own platform
manual_workaround: MSSP watches EDR and identity provider consoles directly; security analysts watch the OT sensors locally
quantified_regulatory_impact: Logs must be captured, stored and protected for the Plan (101.650(c)(1)) and records kept 2 years (101.640)

business_process: Longshore labor ordering and gang timekeeping
description: Order longshore gangs per shift from the hiring halls; record gang hours for billing and labor cost
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Gangs for the next shift must be ordered before the hiring hall deadline; a missed order loses a shift of vessel work
manual_workaround: Order by phone and email to the hiring halls; paper gang sheets entered after recovery
quantified_operational_impact: About 400 to 700 workers ordered a day
